title: NOAA: bleaching is expelled algae, and the coral is not necessarily dead
summary: NOAA says stressed corals expel the symbiotic algae and turn white, and that a bleached coral can still be alive.
body: NOAA says that when corals are stressed by changes in conditions such as temperature, light, or nutrients, they expel the symbiotic algae living in their tissues and turn completely white. It says that when a coral bleaches, it is not dead. It says corals can survive a bleaching event, but they are under more stress and are subject to mortality. The page states the mechanism and that survival is possible. It does not give a death rate.
